Students & Young Professionals (18–34 years old) - Often struggle with inconsistent sleep schedules due to studying, social life, or work. Many live in small dorms or apartments with poor natural light. Low adoption of AI curtains due to rental constraints or affordability concerns. Tech-savvy and more likely to try innovative solutions.

Sleep Improvement Seekers (All Ages) - Includes insomniacs, light sleepers, and those suffering from sleep disorders. Likely already buying melatonin, white noise machines, or wake-up lights. Open to trying new sleep technology to optimize rest.

Daytime Workers & Shift Workers - Many struggle with irregular sleep patterns due to work schedules. AI curtains don't help them because they need controlled artificial daylight. Strong need for circadian rhythm alignment and portable light therapy.
